pick.headline: Polish security officers abduct Father Jerzy Popieluszko
pick.summary: On October 19, 1984, three officers of Poland's Interior Ministry security service abducted Father Jerzy Popieluszko, a priest who supported Solidarity. His body was found in a reservoir eleven days later.
pick.significance: The murder caused national outrage. In an unprecedented trial, the officers and their superior were convicted, exposing the secret police's methods to public view.
pick.fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of October 22, 1984, carried Warsaw Television's account of Father Popieluszko's kidnapping near Torun by men posing as traffic militia, the driver's escape, a car with false plates, and an appeal for witnesses.

alternates.headline: Maurice Bishop killed in Grenada coup
alternates.summary: On October 19, 1983, Grenadian Prime Minister Maurice Bishop and several ministers were executed by soldiers loyal to a hard-line faction of his own party.
alternates.significance: The killing gave the Reagan administration its grounds to invade Grenada six days later.
alternates.fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of October 20, 1983, listed Grenada items under its Caribbean heading, including the Bishop-Coard struggle, "Bishop, Ministers Dead," Austin announcing Bishop's death, and a military government proclamation.

alternates.headline: Moscow expels five US diplomats in spy dispute
alternates.summary: On October 19, 1986, the Soviet Union ordered five American diplomats to leave, in retaliation for the US expulsion of Soviet officials it accused of espionage.
alternates.significance: The tit-for-tat expulsions came days after the Reykjavik summit and escalated into the largest diplomatic expulsion of the Cold War.
alternates.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of October 22, 1986, carried Moscow TASS in English: Gerasimov said five US diplomats declared persona non grata on October 19 had misused their status, and that the tit-for-tat "game" should end.
